solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Date breaks up over comedian, a stinker!

indicators.note: the first word's letters split apart and sit over and around the comedian

parts.note: to date someone is to see them, so the verb gives SEE
a wag is a joker or wit

explanation.surface: A dinner date ruined by a comedian who turns out to be thoroughly unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a stinker' looks like a verdict on the comedian but is the definition: raw waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw waste from drains is the classic foul smell, so it is a fair description of something that reeks.

clue.text: Ship that carries sherry

definitions.meaning: a sailing vessel with fore-and-aft rigging on two or more masts
a tall glass used for serving sherry or beer

explanation.surface: A vessel transporting a cargo of Spanish fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a schooner is also a large sherry glass, so the 'ship' that carries sherry is the glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a two-masted sailing craft and a large glass for fortified wine.

clue.text: Slow time entering manoeuvres before beginning to stop

indicators.note: the time letter goes into the word for tricks

parts.note: wiles are cunning tricks or manoeuvres

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Slow traffic manoeuvring before coming to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow' reads as a driving instruction but means stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow in the sense of dim-witted is a synonym for brainless or foolish.

clue.text: Muck on smoother bird

parts.note: goo is sticky muck or slime
a sander is a tool for smoothing wood

explanation.surface: Grime sitting on a smoothing tool, then a bird appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The goosander is a large fish-eating duck of the merganser family.

clue.text: Happy community going nowhere

parts.note: EC is the European Community
something static is not moving at all

explanation.surface: A contented community that never changes or progresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Overjoyed and delighted, a much stronger form of being pleased.

clue.text: Case of quite curious men or otherwise finding something to eat

indicators.note: these letters are put in another order, made otherwise
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Curious men, or perhaps not, finding food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges QE (the outside of 'quite') with CURIOUSMENOR.
explanation.definitionFit: This French toasted ham and cheese sandwich is a café snack, so it is food.

clue.text: A shocker in Lolita — seriously?

indicators.note: the letters needed lie within the words that follow, across the gap

explanation.surface: A reader asks whether Nabokov's novel Lolita is truly shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: This stun gun delivers an electric shock, so it is literally something that shocks.

clue.text: After launch of Titanic, ship set off

indicators.note: the ship word comes after the letter from the liner
the launch of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a rigger is a ship with a particular rig, as in square-rigger

explanation.surface: After the Titanic was launched, a ship departed.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb or alarm is to activate it, a synonym.

clue.text: Coin box filled with treasure, ultimately

indicators.note: the box contains the next letter

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A coin box stuffed with treasure in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coin' looks like money but is a verb: to coin a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a word is to invent it, a synonym for making something new.

clue.text: Piece inspiring outsiders in Kent to contain this team

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the piece takes the rest inside

parts.note: a particle is a tiny piece

indicators.note: the outside letters of the county hold the next word
the outer letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: A piece encouraging outsiders in Kent to rein in a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' literally means breathing in, so the piece takes the rest inside. Partick Thistle is a Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish football club plays in Glasgow, an example of a sports side.

clue.text: Even bits of warthog added to stew a contentious issue

indicators.note: the letters from the animal are put after the stew

parts.note: a hotpot is a Lancashire stew of meat and sliced potatoes

indicators.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A recipe: put warthog pieces into a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: HOTPOT is a slow-cooked British stew topped with potato.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a controversial question that everyone wants to pass on quickly.

clue.text: Mean party hosts ending in opposition

indicators.note: the party word takes in the letter like a host

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or contest

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A stingy political party welcomes the final part of the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the sense of nasty and spiteful, a synonym of sneering remarks.

clue.text: Exaggerate role in very particular period during month

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the month

parts.note: OCT is the abbreviation for October
an era is a particular period of history

explanation.surface: An actor hamming it up in a very specific month.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham it up, overdoing a part on stage, is an exact paraphrase.

clue.text: Winning Conservative, honourable

parts.note: UP means ahead in a game, as in two goals up
the political right is the conservative side

explanation.surface: A Conservative who wins an election and is a decent person.
explanation.definitionFit: A morally upstanding person is honest and principled, a synonym.

clue.text: Relieved while in action, the first to leave

indicators.note: the word for while goes inside what is left
the opening letter of the word departs

parts.note: a deed is an action
as means while, as in 'as he spoke'

explanation.surface: Relief while the first person leaves the action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'while' is a conjunction here, and the shortened action word wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased in the sense of lessened pain or worry, synonym of soothed.

clue.text: Focus of social activity affected passion

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected or exaggerated
fire means ardour or passion

explanation.surface: A social event where emotions are theatrical and passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: At a camp the gathering takes place round the blaze, where people sing and chat.

clue.text: Signal far off in cross-Channel mix-up

indicators.note: something off is wrong or not right, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A signal from far away garbled across the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: This hybrid jargon blends French with English words, a mixture across the water dividing the two countries.

clue.text: Something sweet I put inside message

indicators.note: the letters go within the word for message

parts.note: a note is a short message
set means put, as in set it down

explanation.surface: A love note with a sweet slipped inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazelnut chocolate confection, an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Vermin in a skirt, you might say, working for cabinetmaker

parts.words: Vermin in a skirt, you might say
parts.note: a rodent in a skirt would be a female one, playfully a she-rat
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: Someone joking about rodents in skirts while at work for a furniture maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English furniture designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was a famous English furniture designer, so he is an example of a cabinet maker.

clue.text: Nurse pulling up underwear in time

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear

explanation.surface: A nurse adjusting underwear in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' is a verb: to nurse a grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a grudge is to keep it alive and cherish it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Sound heart in Paul, Christian for the most part?

indicators.note: the heart of the name is its two middle letters
the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Christian Dior was the French fashion designer

explanation.surface: Paul, a Christian, asks whether his heart is sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' is not a believer but the designer Dior, cut to DIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound broadcasting or recording, as opposed to visual material, is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Shut down company to get things into shape?

parts.note: an engine dies when it shuts down
the cast is the company of actors in a play

explanation.surface: Closing a company to get the business in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal casting in a mould forms objects into a shape, so the question mark flags the literal sense.

clue.text: Rogue needing skill to communicate

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rogue
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A rascal who needs talent to get a message across.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on news or knowledge to someone is a synonym for conveying it.

clue.text: Drink — bird needing one

parts.note: the house martin is a bird
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A thirsty bird wanting just one drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin and vermouth cocktail, an example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Penning memoir finally, enthusiastic about the first few words

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the word holds the letter

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: An author writing a memoir, keen on getting the opening right.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of introduction, the opening remarks before the main text.

clue.text: French artist succeeded, making an entrance

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French neoclassical painter
S is an abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A French painter succeeds in making a grand entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for the act of going in, or the way in, a synonym of entry.

clue.text: A measure in progress

parts.note: a foot is a measure of length

explanation.surface: A measure being worked on right now.
explanation.definitionFit: Something underway or happening now is said to be on foot, a synonym.

clue.text: Outfit with a tanga extremely ludicrous? Completely!

indicators.note: something ludicrous is absurd and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: the extreme letters of the word, its first and last

explanation.surface: Someone declares an outfit with a tiny bikini thong totally absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ludicrous' rearranges OUTFIT, A and TA (the ends of 'tanga'). A tanga is a skimpy bikini bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means entirely or absolutely, as used by English speakers too.

clue.text: Pastry sales?

definitions.meaning: a folded pastry case with a filling, such as an apple one
a business's total revenue from sales over a period

explanation.surface: A bakery owner wonders how pastries are selling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a folded pie and a firm's volume of business.

clue.text: Fly set to buzz around repeatedly

indicators.note: the rearranged trio is given twice over
the letters fly about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A fly is ready to buzz around again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to buzz around' turns SET into TSE, and 'repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: This African biting insect spreads sleeping sickness, an example of a fly.
